Contract allows strides but kernel assumes contiguous; we can call .contiguous() if input is not contiguous to be safe. Output same shape as input, empty_like.

For custom_flatten: accept x, start_dim. The launcher only copies numel elements; flattening from start_dim=1 is guaranteed by input shape and contiguous memory, but to be safe and match contract, we make input contiguous if needed and produce output with shape [batch, -1] where -1 = prod of dims start_dim..end. We call launcher with output.size(0)*output.size(1) elements? Actually launcher copies numel elements exactly, so we can pass input.numel() and allocate output with same numel. Ensure output is contiguous. Return tensor with computed shape.

For custom_linear: accept x, weight, bias (optional Tensor). Validate all CUDA, float32; x and weight contiguous? Contract allows strides but knernel uses raw pointers assuming row-major contiguous. We can call .contiguous() on x and weight if needed. If bias is not None, ensure contiguous. Call launcher with N=x.size(0), in_features=x.size(1), out_features=weight.size(0). Output shape [N, out_features].
Include necessary headers: torch/types.h, torch/csrc/utils/pybind.h, cuda_runtime.h, c10/cuda/CUDAStream.h, ../binding_registry.h. Use extern "C" for all launchers.
Use REGISTER_BINDING(custom_ops, register_custom_ops) to register all functions under one name.
